which can lead to type conflicts and unexpected behavior across your codebase. If you need to add custom properties to

How do I use this without a bundler like Webpack?
Make sure your code is running as a JavaScript module (ESM), for example by using a
HTML document. Then Ky can be imported directly by that module without a bundler or other tools.
Got is maintained by the same people as Ky, so you probably want Ky instead. It’s smaller, works in the browser too, and is
more stable since it’s built on Fetch.
Axios predates the Fetch API and has a lot of legacy baggage. Ky is built on Fetch, which means it’s smaller, more
standards-compliant, and works everywhere Fetch does (browsers, Node.js, Bun, Deno). Ky also has a more modern API
It’s just a random short npm package name I managed to get. It does, however, have a meaning in Japanese:
A form of text-able slang, KY is an abbreviation for 空気読めない (kuuki yomenai), which literally translates into “cannot
read the air.” It’s a phrase applied to someone who misses the implied meaning.
